source_evidence.anchor: equation (1), nearest-rounding definition, and FastTwoSum listing
source_evidence.observation: [PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: equation (1), nearest-rounding definition, and FastTwoSum listing] The paper defines F = {m β^e : m,e ∈ Z, −β^p < m < β^p, e_min ≤ e ≤ e_max}; unadorned arithmetic denotes exact real arithmetic, while circled operations are obtained through fl. Unless stated otherwise, fl selects a nearest member of F. FastTwoSum computes s = x ⊕ y, t = s ⊖ x, and e = y ⊖ t.

[PDF p. 3, printed p. 385, anchor: Section 2, multiple representations] A floating-point value can have several representations m β^e satisfying equation (1), so an exponent e(x) used in a FastTwoSum condition need not be canonical.

[PDF p. 4, printed p. 386, anchor: equation (4), definition of ulp] For r ∈ (−β^(e_max+p), β^(e_max+p)), ulp(r) is min{g−f : f,g ∈ F ∪ {β^(e_max+p)}, f ≤ |r| < g}; for nonnegative x ∈ F it is the distance to the successor.

[PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, anchor: Theorem 2 and condition (7)] FastTwoSum is error-free for nearest addition and faithful subtraction if some representation of its first input x satisfies |y| ≤ ⌈β^p − β/2⌉ β^e(x). The delimiters in condition (7) are ceiling brackets.

[PDF p. 9, printed p. 391, anchor: Section 4 standing assumptions] Section 4 inherits the notation of equation (1), evaluates arithmetic in rounding to nearest unless otherwise specified, and generally assumes absence of overflow. Base restrictions and underflow exceptions are to be stated case by case.

[PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, anchor: FourSumThreeProduct algorithm and TwoProduct introduction] FourSumThreeProduct performs TwoProduct(x2,x3), then TwoProduct(x1,t_h), then TwoProduct(x1,t_l), producing s1,s2',s3',s4'. The paper states that TwoProduct is an error-free two-term product transformation when neither underflow nor overflow occurs.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (17), ThreeProduct listing, Lemma 4, and equation (18)
source_evidence.observation: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (17), ThreeProduct listing, Lemma 4, and equation (18)] Equation (17) gives t_h+t_l=x2·x3, t_h=x2⊙x3, and |t_l|≤(1/2)ulp(x2·x3), with corresponding contracts for the other two TwoProduct calls. ThreeProduct merges s2',s3' using FastTwoSum and sets s3=s3''⊕s4'. Lemma 4 assumes absence of underflow errors within FourSumThreeProduct and concludes ∑_{i=1}^3 s_i=∏_{i=1}^3 x_i.

source_evidence.anchor: proof of Lemma 4, condition (7) and exact final addition
source_evidence.observation: [PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: proof of Lemma 4, condition (7) and exact final addition] The proof constructs a representation of s2' for which condition (7), with its ceiling, holds for FastTwoSum(s2',s3'), obtaining s2+s3''=s2'+s3'. It then proves |s3''+s4'|≤β^p and that this sum lies in F, so s3=s3''+s4' without rounding error.

binders: [PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: equation (1)] Fix the scalar floating-point system F determined by base β, mantissa length p, and exponent bounds e_min,e_max.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: ThreeProduct listing and Lemma 4] Quantify over three scalar inputs x1,x2,x3 ∈ F and let s1,s2,s3 ∈ F be the values computed by ThreeProduct(x1,x2,x3).

[PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchor: FourSumThreeProduct and ThreeProduct listings] Let t_h,t_l,s2',s3',s4',s3'' denote the computed intermediate floating-point values named by those listings.
hypotheses: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 391, anchor: Section 4 standing assumptions] All arithmetic operations used here are rounded to nearest unless the passage states otherwise.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 391, anchor: Section 4 standing assumptions] Overflow is absent throughout the application.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: Lemma 4 hypothesis] There are no underflow errors within the FourSumThreeProduct call.

[PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchor: TwoProduct paragraph and equation (17)] Each of the three delegated TwoProduct calls obeys its error-free high-plus-low product contract under the inherited range assumptions.
conclusions: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: Lemma 4 and equation (18)] The computed outputs satisfy the exact real identity s1+s2+s3=x1·x2·x3, equivalently ∑_{i=1}^3 s_i=∏_{i=1}^3 x_i.
[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: condition (7) in the proof of Lemma 4] The FastTwoSum merge is exact: s2+s3''=s2'+s3'.
[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: final paragraph of the proof of Lemma 4] The final floating-point addition is exact: s3=s3''⊕s4'=s3''+s4'.

[PDF pp. 14–15, printed pp. 396–397, anchor: ThreeProduct motivation and proof of Lemma 4] Consequently the four-term error-free decomposition produced by FourSumThreeProduct is reduced to a three-term error-free decomposition without an additional rounding error.
definitions_and_conventions: [PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: equation (1)] F consists only of real values mβ^e with integer m,e, strict mantissa bounds −β^p<m<β^p, and inclusive exponent bounds e_min≤e≤e_max.

[PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: floating-point operation semantics] A circled operation such as ⊕ or ⊙ denotes a computed floating-point result; ordinary + and · in the identities denote exact real operations.
[PDF p. 4, printed p. 386, anchor: equation (4)] ulp is the absolute spacing notion defined by equation (4), not a relative-error measure.

[PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchor: FourSumThreeProduct and equation (17)] The first TwoProduct call has t_h+t_l=x2·x3, t_h=x2⊙x3, and |t_l|≤(1/2)ulp(x2·x3); the phrase 'respective conditions for line 2 and 3' applies the analogous exact-decomposition and half-ULP-residual properties to x1·t_h and x1·t_l.

[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: ThreeProduct listing] Prime marks are semantic: s2',s3',s4' are FourSumThreeProduct terms, s3'' is the residual returned by FastTwoSum(s2',s3'), and s3 is the result of adding s3'' to s4'.
implicit_context: [PDF p. 9, printed p. 391, anchor: Section 4 standing assumptions] The result inherits β,p,e_min,e_max and the operation notation from the earlier sections.

[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: paragraph preceding ThreeProduct] No restriction to β∈{2,3} is imposed for this application; the proof establishes condition (7) for the relevant FastTwoSum call for an unrestricted floating-point base β.

[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: paragraph preceding ThreeProduct] No ordering hypothesis such as |s2'|≥|s3'| or ulp(s2')≥ulp(s3') is assumed; the paper explicitly notes that these inequalities need not hold.

[PDF pp. 14–15, printed pp. 396–397, anchor: proof normalization] The proof's scaling to ulp(x_i)=1, integrality of the scaled x_i, and max{|x1|,|x2|,|x3|}≤β^p−1 is a without-loss-of-generality proof device, not an additional input restriction.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: proof of Lemma 4] The case x1x2x3=0 is treated as trivial and remains included in the result.
statement.algorithm_linkage: [PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchors: FourSumThreeProduct and ThreeProduct listings] The exact variant is: (t_h,t_l)←TwoProduct(x2,x3); (s1,s2')←TwoProduct(x1,t_h); (s3',s4')←TwoProduct(x1,t_l); (s2,s3'')←FastTwoSum(s2',s3'); s3←s3''⊕s4'. It uses the ordinary FastTwoSum, not cβ-FastTwoSum, and the product grouping starts with x2·x3.
numerical_model: [PDF pp. 2 and 9, printed pp. 384 and 391, anchors: nearest-rounding definition and Section 4 standing assumptions] Every displayed computed operation is in the single p-digit system F and uses rounding to nearest under the inherited convention.

[PDF p. 5, printed p. 387, anchor: Theorem 2] The exactness result invoked for the merge requires nearest addition and faithful subtraction; nearest-rounded subtraction supplied by the standing convention is a faithful subtraction.

[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (17)] The high product t_h is a rounded product, while t_h+t_l is the exact product x2·x3; the same high-plus-residual distinction is inherited for the other TwoProduct calls.
[PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: nearest-rounding definition] The source's nearest-rounding condition permits either nearest value in a tie and does not state a tie-breaking rule.
error_notions: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (17)] TwoProduct's low component is an exact residual with an absolute half-ULP bound, for example |t_l|≤(1/2)ulp(x2·x3).

[PDF pp. 14–15, printed pp. 396–397, anchor: Lemma 4 and its proof] 'Error-free' means exact equality of the unevaluated sum of the returned floating-point components with the exact real triple product.
[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: exact merge and final-add proof] The merge and final addition introduce zero additional error.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (18)] Lemma 4 states no relative-error, backward-error, or componentwise accuracy bound for the final three components beyond their exact-sum identity.
norms: [PDF pp. 14–15, printed pp. 396–397, anchors: equation (17) and proof bounds] Only scalar absolute value |·| and ulp-based scalar bounds occur; no vector or matrix norm is involved.
constants_and_indexing: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equations (17) and (18)] Input and output indices run exactly from 1 through 3; the intermediate FourSum decomposition uses s1 and s_i' for i=2,3,4.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (17)] The TwoProduct residual constant is exactly 1/2 and the inequality is non-strict: |t_l|≤(1/2)ulp(x2·x3).
[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: intermediate bounds in the proof] Under the proof normalization, |s2'|≤(1/2)β^(2p), |s3'|≤(1/2)β^(2p), and |s4'|≤(1/2)β^p.

[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: verification of condition (7)] The exact coefficient used in condition (7) is the ceiling ⌈β^p−β/2⌉, not a floor; the proof obtains |s3'|≤⌈β^p−β/2⌉β^e(s2') for a suitable representation of s2'.
[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: final-add bound] The proof uses |s3''|≤(1/2)β^p and |s4'|≤(1/2)β^p, hence |s3''+s4'|≤β^p, all with non-strict inequalities.
higher_order_terms: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (18)] There are no omitted terms, asymptotic terms, or big-O remainders: the conclusion is an exact finite identity.
exceptional_values: [PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: equation (1)] F is a set of finite real floating-point values; NaNs and signed infinities are not members of the modeled domain.
[PDF p. 9, printed p. 391, anchor: Section 4 standing assumptions] Overflow is excluded.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: Lemma 4 hypothesis] Underflow errors are excluded specifically within FourSumThreeProduct.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: proof of Lemma 4] Zero inputs and the case x1x2x3=0 are not excluded.

undebatable_constraints: [PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchors: algorithm listings] The algorithm must use exactly three TwoProduct calls with product order (x2,x3), (x1,t_h), and (x1,t_l), followed by FastTwoSum(s2',s3') and the addition s3''⊕s4'.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (18)] The required result is exact equality s1+s2+s3=x1x2x3, not an approximation bound on a rounded total.

[PDF pp. 9 and 14, printed pp. 391 and 396, anchors: standing assumptions and Lemma 4] Absence of overflow is inherited, and absence of underflow errors inside FourSumThreeProduct is an explicit hypothesis.
[PDF pp. 14–15, printed pp. 396–397, anchors: condition (7) discussion and proof] The ordinary FastTwoSum is used without a β∈{2,3} restriction and without magnitude or ULP ordering of s2',s3'.

[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: verification of condition (7)] Any formal reconstruction of the merge condition must preserve the ceiling ⌈β^p−β/2⌉ and the existential choice of a representation of s2'.
[PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: final paragraph of the proof] The final operation s3''⊕s4' must be represented as exact under the proved bound, not merely nearest-rounded with a nonzero error.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: equation (17)] TwoProduct high values are computed rounded products, while the associated high-plus-low sums equal exact real products.
[PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: proof normalization] The normalization ulp(x_i)=1 and integrality bounds are proof-local and must not be imposed as hypotheses on the original inputs.

ambiguities.issue: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: Lemma 4 hypothesis] The phrase 'absence of underflow errors' is not formally defined in this passage.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchors: TwoProduct paragraph and Lemma 4] The surrounding prose first says TwoProduct is error-free if neither underflow nor overflow occurs, while Lemma 4 uses the narrower wording 'absence of underflow errors within the FourSumThreeProduct call.'
ambiguities.impact: [PDF p. 14, printed p. 396, anchor: Lemma 4] A formalization should preserve the stated no-underflow-error condition or separately justify strengthening it to absence of every underflow event.

ambiguities.issue: [PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchors: TwoProduct introduction and equation (17)] The internal implementation variant of TwoProduct is not specified.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 13, printed p. 395, anchor: TwoProduct introduction] The paper identifies TwoProduct as a known algorithm and supplies its behavioral contract, but does not select an FMA-based, splitting-based, or other concrete implementation.
ambiguities.impact: [PDF pp. 13–14, printed pp. 395–396, anchors: TwoProduct contract] The source contract constrains TwoProduct by its rounded-high, exact-decomposition, and half-ULP properties rather than by a particular instruction sequence.

ambiguities.issue: [PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: nearest-rounding definition] Tie-breaking for rounding to nearest is unspecified.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 2, printed p. 384, anchor: nearest-rounding inequality] fl(r) is required only to be at least as close to r as every f∈F; no ties-to-even or ties-away convention is named.
ambiguities.impact: [PDF pp. 14–15, printed pp. 396–397, anchor: Lemma 4 proof] The claimed exactness must hold independently of which nearest value is chosen in a tie.

ambiguities.issue: [PDF pp. 3 and 15, printed pp. 385 and 397, anchors: multiple representations and condition (7) proof] The exponent e(s2') used to establish the FastTwoSum condition is representation-dependent.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: representation of s2'] The proof states that there exists a representation of s2' satisfying β^e(s2')≥ulp(t_h), consistent with the earlier non-uniqueness of floating-point representations.
ambiguities.impact: [PDF p. 15, printed p. 397, anchor: condition (7)] A formalization must use an existentially suitable representation or prove that its chosen exponent convention supplies the required inequality.

contract_plain_english: [PDF pp. 9 and 13–15, printed pp. 391 and 395–397, anchors: Section 4 assumptions, ThreeProduct listing, Lemma 4, and its proof] For any three scalar floating-point inputs, under nearest-rounded arithmetic, no overflow, and no underflow errors in the three-call FourSumThreeProduct stage, ThreeProduct first obtains the standard four-term exact decomposition, merges its middle two terms with ordinary FastTwoSum, and exactly adds the merge residual to the fourth term. No base restriction or magnitude ordering is required. The three returned floating-point numbers have an exact real sum equal to x1x2x3, with no omitted error term.
